summary: Helio Search (Dedicated): sustained throughput below expectation during peak hours (decode tokens/sec dips, increased queueing)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports sustained throughput below contracted/expected levels during peak hours (roughly 16:00–19:00 ET) on their Dedicated deployment.
- Symptoms: slower streaming, longer time-to-first-token (TTFT) and overall completion time, with backlog/queueing. Customer sees no explicit 429s in their client, but notes requests “hang” longer.

Customer impact
- Production-facing search assistant degraded during peak traffic window; customer reports ~20–35% drop in throughput compared to their steady-state baseline.
- Customer is concerned guarantee is not being met and requests immediate mitigation + clear explanation of whether this is an SLO breach vs expected throttling.

Customer-provided details (initial)
- Deployment: Dedicated (single pool), us-east
- Model: rw-openchat-70b-instruct
- Traffic pattern: bursty concurrency increases at top-of-hour; mix of prompt sizes (customer says “mostly 1–4k input tokens”, but some longer)
- Streaming: enabled
- Time window: 2025-02-10 21:00–00:00 UTC (approx 16:00–19:00 ET)

Initial triage performed (Support)
1) Checked Dedicated Throughput SLO dashboard (internal beta) for deployment_id provided by CS.
   - Dashboard: https://grafana.prod.us-east.redwoodinference.com/d/ded-throughput-slo/dedicated-throughput-slo?var-deployment_id=ded-helio-prod-07
   - Observed:
     - Effective output_tokens_per_sec declines during reported window.
     - Queue depth and scheduler wait time increase.
     - Throttling signals are present (admission control) but not dominant; no large spike in explicit 429s at gateway.
2) Checked saturation signals:
   - GPU utilization near sustained high-water mark.
   - Prefill time distribution widened (p95), decode steady but slowed when queue depth peaks.
3) Cross-checked fleet events:
   - No full-region GPU incident; did note a node maintenance/drain event on one worker in the pool within the timeframe (needs confirmation from Infra).

Hypotheses
- Autoscaling / capacity headroom insufficient for their burst profile (min replicas too low; scale-up lag) causing queue build-up and apparent throughput drop.
- Prompt-length distribution heavier than assumed (more long-prefill requests) causing effective tokens/sec to fall below customer’s expectation (esp. under concurrency).
- Possible contention in their dedicated pool due to node drain or partial capacity reduction during maintenance.
- Admission control may be protecting tail latency by limiting concurrency (customer may interpret as throughput loss).

What we need from customer to confirm
- 3–5 example request_ids from the affected window.
- Approximate concurrency during peak (or their client-side queue length).
- Confirmation of prompt length distribution (p50/p95 input tokens) and output token cap.
- Whether they recently changed any settings: max_tokens, streaming, tool/function calling, response format constraints.

Next steps / actions
- SRE/Infra to confirm any capacity reduction/maintenance events on the dedicated pool during the reported window.
- Runtime/Scheduler to review queue depth + prefill/decode spans for the specific deployment to determine if this is capacity-limited vs policy-limited.
- If capacity-limited: propose immediate mitigation (temporary min replicas increase / add 1 node / enable burst capacity) and longer-term tier/shape recommendation.
- If policy-limited: align customer on expected behavior (throttling vs breach) and adjust admission control/burst policy if appropriate.

Notes
- Customer requested “a clear answer” on whether the guarantee is tokens/sec or req/sec. We pointed them to our internal standard and will provide customer-facing explanation once we confirm exact tier/contract language for their account.

resolution: Pending customer confirmation to apply mitigation (temporary capacity add / burst). Root cause suspected: capacity saturation due to increased peak concurrency and max_output_tokens, compounded by a worker replacement event causing temporary capacity reduction.
